newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas stages major rally in the West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Hamas stages major rally in the West Bank.

text.p: Thousands of Hamas supporters packed a soccer field in the West Bank on Friday to send the message that the militant Islamic group is back at the centre of Palestinian political life.

About 20,000 supporters filled the Nablus municipal field to mark last month's ninth anniversary of the group and the first anniversary of the January 5, 1996 assassination of Hamas master bombmaker Yahya Ayyash, allegedly killed by Israel.

The rally was one of the largest in the West Bank since Hamas resumed public activity following crackdowns by the Palestinian Authority and Israel after suicide bombings last February and March killed 59 people in Israel.
"The movement emerged from the campaign of repression more coherent, more able to speak for itself and unshaken in its vision," said Jamal Mansour, a leader of Hamas in Nablus.
"Some may think that Hamas's light has been dimmed. But with God's help it has grown more in strength," he said.

Hamas, the main opponent to Israeli-PLO peace moves faced its most testing time in 1996 when Israel and the Palestinian Authority rounded up more than 2,000 activists and supporters following the Islamic suicide bombings.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's Authority nearly destroyed the Hamas infrastructure when it shut many social, health and educational institutions and wrenched control of mosques once run by Hamas in Gaza.
But the group, dubbed by some as the mythical hydra for its ability to spring back, appeared undaunted as it returned to the centre of Palestinian political life.
Activists boasted that those attending Friday's rally came only from the Nablus district, excluding other parts of the West Bank.

Palestinian police stood outside the field, which was decorated with pictures of the wheelchair-bound founder and spiritual leader of Hamas, Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, who is serving a life sentence in an Israeli prison.

One portrait depicted Yassin on an eagle gripping an octopus marked with Israel's symbol, the Star of David, in its claws. The eagle was trying to take the octopus from a burning Dome of the Rock, the mosque that stands on Islam's third holiest site.
Leaders of Hamas spoke defiantly of Israeli-PLO peace moves, saying the impasse over an overdue Israeli army withdrawal from most of the West Bank town of Hebron justifies the group's position.

"Hamas has from the start said that the conditions for the (peace) process were not right because the scale was tipped in favour of our enemy," Ahmed al-Haj Ali, a Hamas leader, read from the group's official speech.
"The latest events and developments in the course of the political process attest to the truth of our outlook and the correctness of our analysis," he said.

Haj Ali beamed as he peered down at the packed field from a stage decorated with pictures of the Dome of the Rock flanked by portraits of Yassin, Ayyash and Mousa Abu Marzuk, a Hamas leader jailed in the United States.

The crowd broke into applause each time the name of Ayyash, nicknamed the "Engineer", was mentioned. Ayyash's father ignited cheers when he took the stage carrying the "Engineer's" three-year-old son Bara'.
Hamas activists said the rally showed that the group had overcome last year's crackdown and was resuming its role as an opposition political group.
